newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan June leading indicators likely below 50 -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan June leading indicators likely below 50 -- EPA.

text.p: Japan's diffusion index of leading economic indicators for June is likely to be below the "boom-or-bust" mark of 50, an Economic Planning Agency (EPA) official told reporters on Tuesday.

"The coincident indicator will probably be over 50 (in June), taking into account the forecast for production. There is a good possibility, however, that leading indicators will be the same as they were in May," he said when asked if leading indicators for June were also expected to be below 50.
Earlier on Tuesday, the EPA announced that the index for leading indicators in May was 33.3.

The fact that the index of leading indicators has been below 50 for several months does not necessarily mean, however, that Japan's economy is going to slow down in the near future, the official added.

He attributed the May index of leading indicators being below 50 for a fifth consecutive month to a comparatively high reading in February, due to a rush of consumer buying before the increase in Japan's consumption tax on April 1.
The index is calculated by comparing trends in the prior three months, which for the May index would have included February, March and April.

The official said it was difficult to be certain whether the effect of the consumption tax increase on leading indicators would dissipate after the June figure, although the effect was certain to dissipate in the coming months.
